title: Allah swears by everything you can see.
subtitle: The visible world as a witness
then: The second part of the surah turns to the Quran itself. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}swears by His creation, in which His signs can be seen{/idea}, and which {reward}show the perfection of His Names and Attributes.{/reward}
now: The sunrise through the kitchen window. Your baby's fingers. The rain on the car roof. {idea}Everything you see is a witness.{/idea} The oath asks you to look again.
old: What I see every day is ordinary.
new: Everything I see is a sign of Allah, sworn by as a witness.
try: Stop once today and look closely at one ordinary thing. Say subhanAllah.

title: And by everything you cannot see.
subtitle: Most of reality is hidden from you
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah then {idea}swears by the hidden things they cannot see.{/idea} Both oaths together confirm one thing: {reward}the Quran is His Speech and revelation.{/reward}
now: Wi-Fi, gravity, the air in your lungs. You cannot see any of it, and you rely on all of it. {idea}The unseen is not unreal.{/idea} Angels, the soul, the Hereafter belong to it too.
old: If I cannot see it, I find it hard to believe.
new: Much of what is most real is unseen, and Allah swears by it.
try: Think of one unseen blessing you depend on today, and thank Allah for it.

title: This is the word of a noble Messenger.
subtitle: What the oath is sworn for
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word messenger {idea}carries the meaning of conveying{/idea}, because a messenger delivers from the sender. In Surat At-Takwir it is used for Jibril, here for {reward}Muhammad ﷺ, who carried the trust faithfully.{/reward}
now: A courier brings you a letter. You do not think the words are his. {idea}The Quran came through noble messengers{/idea}, delivered without change. {reward}It is a letter to you.{/reward}
old: The Quran is a book written by a man.
new: It is Allah's word, delivered faithfully by noble messengers.
try: Before reading Quran today, remind yourself: this is Allah speaking to me.

title: Not the word of a poet. Little do you believe.
subtitle: The verse that answered Umar's thought
then: The surah introduction tells that Umar, before Islam, stood behind the Prophet ﷺ as he recited this surah. Amazed at its beauty, Umar thought {trap}he must be a poet{/trap}, and just then he heard: {idea}it is not the word of a poet.{/idea}
now: You hear a recitation and feel it is beautiful, like a good song. {trap}It is easy to stop at the sound.{/trap} {idea}The beauty is there to carry you to the meaning.{/idea}
old: The Quran is beautiful, like great poetry.
new: Its beauty is not poetry. It is revelation, asking me to believe.
try: Listen to one short recitation today, then read its meaning.

title: Not a fortune teller either. Little do you reflect.
subtitle: The second answer that reached Umar's heart
then: Umar then thought, {trap}he must be a soothsayer, if not a poet.{/trap} The very next words recited were {idea}nor the word of a soothsayer, little do you reflect.{/idea} Umar said Islam entered deep into his heart.
now: You hear a verse that seems to answer what you were just thinking. {idea}It happens.{/idea} The question is whether you stop and reflect, {trap}or move on to the next video.{/trap}
old: I would believe more if I had more proof.
new: Often what I lack is not proof but reflection.
try: Take one verse you read today and spend five minutes thinking about it.

title: A revelation from the Lord of all the worlds.
subtitle: Where it truly comes from

row.title: revelation
sub: from the Lord of all that exists

then: After the two denials comes the positive answer. Ibn Kathir: {idea}this is the revelation sent down from the Lord of all that exists.{/idea} Umar heard this line and {reward}it stayed in his heart{/reward}, though he believed fully only later.
now: The Quran on your shelf, maybe dusty. The app you open in Ramadan. {idea}It is a message from the Lord of every world.{/idea} {reward}Some seeds take years to grow, like Umar's.{/reward}
old: I will take the Quran seriously when I feel ready.
new: It is from the Lord of the worlds, and even a little attention plants a seed.
try: Open the Quran today and read just one page.

title: Had he made up a single word about Us.
subtitle: The Messenger ﷺ could not invent a thing
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}if Muhammad ﷺ forged something against Us{/trap}, or added or removed anything from the Message, {idea}We would surely be swift in punishing him.{/idea} And of course, {reward}he did not do any of this.{/reward}
now: You pass on a quote you are not sure of. You say the Prophet ﷺ said something you saw in a forwarded message. {trap}It is easy to add to religion.{/trap} {idea}Even the Messenger ﷺ was held to exactness.{/idea}
old: Passing on a nice saying about Islam is harmless.
new: Words attributed to Allah or His Messenger ﷺ must be exact.
try: Before forwarding the next religious quote, check its source first.

title: We would have seized him by the right hand.
subtitle: The strongest grip, to show how serious it is
then: Ibn Kathir says it has been explained that the right hand is mentioned {idea}because it is stronger in grabbing.{/idea} The point is that {reward}Allah Himself guarded the message{/reward}, and the Prophet ﷺ was truthful.
now: You wonder sometimes if what you read was changed over time. {reward}Allah guarded this message from the start{/reward}, even from the one who brought it. {idea}You can trust what you hold.{/idea}
old: Maybe the message was changed along the way.
new: Allah guarded the message so firmly that even its Messenger ﷺ could not alter it.
try: Thank Allah today for preserving the Quran you can open on your phone.

title: Then We would have cut his life artery.
subtitle: The certainty that he spoke only truth
then: Ibn Abbas said al-watin is {idea}the artery attached to the heart.{/idea} Ibn Kathir sums it up: the point is that {reward}he ﷺ is truthful, righteous and guided{/reward}, and Allah helped him with clear proofs.
now: People trust a doctor who has never been caught lying. {reward}The Messenger ﷺ conveyed the message to the end and was never stopped.{/reward} {idea}That itself is a sign of who sent him.{/idea}
old: How can I be sure the Prophet ﷺ spoke the truth?
new: Allah said He would have stopped any lie at once. He never did.
try: Read one hadith about the Prophet's honesty today and share it with someone.

title: And none of you could have shielded him.
subtitle: No one stands between Allah and His decision
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}none of you would be able to come between Us and him{/trap} if We wanted it. The deniers could not have protected him. {idea}And because no one could stop Allah, his safety proved his truth.{/idea}
now: You think the right connections will protect you. The lawyer, the uncle with influence. {trap}No one can stand between you and Allah.{/trap} {idea}So seek protection from Him directly.{/idea}
old: With the right people behind me, I am safe.
new: No one can shield me from Allah. Only He can protect me.
try: Say a short du'a for protection this morning instead of relying only on people.

title: It is a reminder for those mindful of Allah.
subtitle: Who the Quran actually reaches
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran is a reminder for the mindful, and cites: {reward}it is for those who believe a guide and a healing{/reward}, and for those who disbelieve {trap}there is heaviness in their ears.{/trap}
now: Two people hear the same verse on the same radio. One stops and thinks, one changes the station. {idea}The difference is the heart.{/idea} {reward}A little taqwa opens the ears.{/reward}
old: The Quran does not seem to affect me much.
new: The more mindful of Allah I am, the more the Quran reaches me.
try: Before reading or listening to Quran today, ask Allah to open your heart to it.

title: We know some among you will still deny.
subtitle: Clarity does not force belief
then: Ibn Kathir explains that even {idea}with this explanation and clarification{/idea}, there will still be {trap}those who reject the Quran.{/trap} Allah knew it, and told His Messenger ﷺ so.
now: You share a reminder with your family and someone rolls their eyes. You explain your faith to a coworker and it goes nowhere. {idea}Allah already knew some would deny.{/idea} {reward}Your task is to be sincere, not to convince everyone.{/reward}
old: If people do not accept what I share, I failed.
new: Some will deny however clear it is. My part is to share sincerely.
try: Share one good reminder today and let go of how it is received.

title: It will be deep regret for those who reject it.
subtitle: The Quran ignored becomes a sorrow
then: Ibn Jarir said {trap}this rejection will be anguish for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds it may refer to the Quran itself, and cites: {trap}a barrier will be set between them and what they desire.{/trap}
now: The course you never took. The call you never returned. {trap}Regret is for chances missed.{/trap} {reward}The Quran is a chance in your hand right now.{/reward}
old: I can always come back to the Quran later.
new: The Quran I ignore now could become my regret. The Quran I follow becomes my guide.
try: Set a small daily Quran time, even five minutes, starting today.

title: It is the certain truth.
subtitle: No doubt, suspicion, or confusion in it
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}the right and truthful news in which there is no doubt, suspicion or confusion.{/idea} The surah began with al-Haqqah, the inevitable reality, and {reward}closes by calling the Quran the certain truth.{/reward}
now: Headlines change by the hour. Experts reverse themselves. Your feed contradicts itself before lunch. {trap}Certainty is rare.{/trap} {reward}Here is a book with none of that doubt.{/reward}
old: Nothing can really be known for certain.
new: The Quran is truth I can stand on when everything else shifts.
try: When you feel unsure today, read one verse and let it steady you.

title: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
subtitle: The fitting response to all that was said

row.title: close the book and move on

then: Ibn Kathir says this means glorify {idea}the One Who sent down this magnificent Quran.{/idea} After the Day of Judgment, the records, and the truth of the message, {reward}the surah ends with praise.{/reward}
now: You finish a powerful talk and immediately check your phone. {trap}The moment passes.{/trap} {reward}This verse asks you to end with your Lord's name on your tongue.{/reward}
old: After reading, I just move on with my day.
new: The right ending to hearing the truth is glorifying the One who sent it.
try: Say subhana Rabbiyal 'Azim slowly three times right now, then in each ruku' today.
